title: Reading the result: percentiles, throughput, error rate and why the mean misleads

videos.script: A load test ends, and it prints a table. Six hundred and fifty-three requests, and a mean of a hundred and twenty-four and a half milliseconds. {{table}} That sounds like a fact about the box office. It is not a fact about anybody. Only two of those requests took anything close to it. {{histogram}} Half of them took under thirty-two milliseconds. A hundred and thirty-three were bookings, and they waited nearly half a second each. The mean lands in the empty space between them. {{gap}} This lesson reads the result the way the users lived it. Percentiles first, worked by hand on twenty real timings, so you know exactly what p95 means. {{pencil}} Then throughput, and the point where adding workers buys nothing but waiting. {{plateau}} Then errors, and why a refused booking is not one. {{status}} And last, a trap. When the server freezes for a second, a polite load generator stops asking. Its report looks perfect. {{pause}} The users who arrived during that second waited anyway. By the end you will know how to count them. {{users}}
